bodyHtml:
Does five years of fab-shop welding count toward API 510?

Partly, at best, and only API can decide. API's published requirement for a candidate with a high school diploma is three years of design, fabrication, repair, operation or inspection of pressure vessels, of which one year must be supervising or performing inspection activities as described in API 510. Structural welding is not pressure vessel work, so it does not fit that wording. Pressure piping fits API 570's wording better than API 510's. And API states that the experience must have been acquired within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency as defined in API 510. A fabrication shop is not normally an authorized inspection agency, which is why most welders still need a year inside an inspection organization before applying.

This section works through that question in detail, because it is the one welders ask most often and the one training-provider pages tend to answer too optimistically. Everything below is based on API's published qualification wording on api.org at the time of writing. API changes its programmes; check the current requirement page before you apply, and treat API's review of your application as the only authoritative answer.

Reading API's wording clause by clause

API publishes the API 510 requirement as four education tiers. Each tier specifies a number of years and the kind of experience that counts. Breaking the wording into its parts shows exactly where a welder's résumé fits and where it does not.

Part of the requirementWhat API's wording saysWhat it means for a welder
Years by educationOne year with a BS in engineering or technology (or three or more years of technical military service); two years with a two-year degree or certificate (or two years of technical military service); three years with a high school diploma or equivalent; five or more years with no formal educationNo degree is required. A diploma or GED saves two years against the no-education tier.
Type of experienceDesign, fabrication, repair, operation or inspection of pressure vesselsWelding on ASME pressure vessels or vessel repairs fits the words. Structural steel does not. Piping is a different equipment class.
Inspection floorOne year must be in supervision or performance of inspection activities as described in API 510Welding alone can never satisfy this year, however long you have welded.
Recency and employerAcquired within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency as defined in API 510Who you worked for matters as much as what you did. Old experience and non-agency employers are the usual problems.
VerificationExperience must be documented on the application and will be verified; supervisor contact details are requiredVague job titles or unreachable supervisors slow or sink an application.

The degree question, which the page above answers, is the easy part. The harder parts are the type of experience and the employer condition, and they are where a fab-shop welding history needs honest scrutiny.

Structural welding, pressure piping and vessel work: how each maps

The question that sends many welders to this page describes five years in a fabrication shop, mostly structural with some pressure piping. Each slice of that experience maps differently.

Structural welding. Beams, columns, platforms, pipe racks and skids are structural work governed by codes such as AWS D1.1. API's API 510 wording names pressure vessels, so structural welding falls outside it. It is valuable experience for AWS Certified Welding Inspector, where welding-related experience is the qualifying category, but it is not pressure vessel experience.

Pressure piping. Spool fabrication to ASME B31.3 or B31.1 is pressure equipment work, but it is piping, not vessels. API 570 uses different wording: design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of in-service piping systems. Note the words "in-service". New-construction spool welding in a shop is not obviously in-service piping work, so even for API 570 it is uncertain. A welder whose history is mostly piping should still read the API 570 requirement rather than assuming either programme accepts it.

Pressure vessel fabrication and repair. Welding on ASME Section VIII vessels, in a shop that builds them or on vessel repairs and alterations, fits the API 510 description of fabrication or repair of pressure vessels. This is the slice most likely to count toward the non-inspection years, subject to the employer condition below.

Fabrication QC on new vessels. Many welders move into a shop QC role before they move into inspection. That is useful experience and may help an application, but API 510 is an in-service inspection code, and the mandatory inspection year refers to inspection activities as described in API 510. Shop QC on new construction is generally not the same thing. If your QC role included in-service work, such as inspecting repairs on vessels returned from service, document it specifically.

The authorized inspection agency condition, applied to a fab shop

API attaches the employer condition to the qualifying experience as a whole: it must have been gained within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency as defined in API 510. The API 510 definition of an authorized inspection agency covers organizations such as a jurisdictional inspection organization, an insurance carrier's inspection organization, an owner/user's inspection organization for its own equipment, and an independent organization or individual under contract to an owner/user. The exact definition varies slightly between editions, so check the current code.

A typical fabrication shop is none of those. It builds equipment for others and may have its own QC department and an Authorized Inspector from an insurer or the jurisdiction visiting to witness ASME Code work, but the shop itself is not the inspection agency. Read literally, years spent welding in that shop do not meet the employer condition, even where the work was pressure vessels.

The exceptions are worth checking. A welder employed by a refinery or chemical plant maintenance department that sits alongside an owner/user inspection organization may have a different story, as may a welder employed by an inspection company that also performs repairs under contract to an owner/user. These cases depend on facts only API can weigh. The practical rule is to describe your employer, the equipment, the owner you worked for and your duties accurately on the application, and let API make the call. Do not stretch a job description to fit the wording; API verifies experience with your supervisor.

Scenarios: what typical backgrounds are likely to need

The scenarios below are illustrations, not eligibility rulings. They show how API's published wording is likely to apply. API decides every case.

BackgroundHow API's wording appliesRealistic next step
Five years of structural welding in a fab shop, high school diplomaStructural work is not pressure vessel experience; the shop is not an inspection agency; no inspection yearEarn an inspection-side credential, join an inspection organization, build qualifying years there
Five years of pressure vessel welding in an ASME shop, high school diplomaType of work fits the wording; employer condition likely not met; no inspection yearSame as above; the vessel knowledge will help, but qualifying time starts at the inspection employer
Plant maintenance welder at a refinery, high school diplomaRepair of pressure vessels fits; employer may connect to an owner/user inspection organization; inspection year still missingSeek a transfer into the plant's inspection department and log the inspection year
UT technician with an inspection company contracted to refiners, two yearsInspection work under contract to an owner/user is the core case the wording describesConfirm duties map to API 510 inspection activities and that the total meets your education tier
Pipe welder moving into piping inspectionBetter fit for API 570 wording on in-service piping than API 510Read the API 570 requirement and consider it as the first API certification

Documenting experience so API can verify it

API states that the minimum experience must be documented on the application and will be verified, and that candidates must provide contact information for their supervisor. Applications slow down when the description is vague or the supervisor cannot be reached. A strong experience record has the same qualities whether it is reviewed by API, an employer or an auditor:

  • Dates and employer for each role, with the employer's relationship to the equipment owner stated plainly, for example an independent inspection company under contract to a named refinery.
  • Equipment class, naming pressure vessels, heat exchangers, columns or drums rather than "equipment".
  • Duties in inspection language: external and internal examinations, thickness monitoring, assessing corrosion, witnessing repairs, reviewing NDE results. List NDE methods performed and the certifications held at the time.
  • Supervisor details for someone who can confirm the work, ideally the inspector or inspection supervisor you reported to.
  • Contemporaneous records, such as job logs and timesheets kept as you go, rather than a reconstruction years later.

The same habits that satisfy an NDE written practice audit produce an experience record API can verify quickly, which is one reason many technicians keep a running log from their first inspection job.

What happens after you qualify: exam and recertification facts

API currently describes the API 510 examination as a 7.5-hour computer-based exam at Prometric testing centres, with a closed-book section and an open-book section in which the referenced codes and standards are displayed on screen; physical reference materials are not allowed. API lists 170 questions, of which 140 are scored. API announced in August 2024 that remote proctoring is no longer offered for API 510, 570 and 653, so plan for a test-centre appointment. Our API ICP exam delivery guide covers the delivery changes in more detail.

Certification lasts three years. To recertify, API currently requires that at least 20 percent of time in the most recent three-year period be spent performing or supervising inspection, plus continuing professional development hours, and an online open-book quiz every six years. Since September 2025 API accepts CPD documentation only when it shows verifiable instructional contact time or CEUs. The practical point for a career changer is that API 510 is not a one-time hurdle: staying certified requires staying in inspection work.

Canada and the National Board route

In Alberta, ABSA's in-service pressure equipment inspector certification, described in ABSA document AB-526, lists a passing result on the API 510 or API 570 certification examination, or the National Board in-service commission examination, among its prerequisites alongside ABSA's own examination. Owner-users with an ABSA-accepted integrity management system rely on such certified inspectors. Other provinces have their own regulators, so confirm the requirement with ABSA, TSSA in Ontario or the relevant provincial authority before planning a Canadian route.

In the United States, the National Board commission is a separate credential used by jurisdictional and insurance inspectors; it has its own eligibility rules and is not interchangeable with API 510. Our comparison of API 510 and the National Board commission explains the difference.

Common mistakes welders make with the API 510 application

  • Counting all welding years. Only experience that fits the pressure vessel wording and the employer condition counts.
  • Applying to the wrong programme. A piping-heavy background may fit API 570 better than API 510.
  • Letting experience age out. Experience older than 10 years does not count under API's recency wording.
  • Treating fabrication QC as in-service inspection. Describe it accurately and let API judge it.
  • Buying exam preparation before confirming eligibility. Check API's requirement and your records first.
  • Skipping method certification. Inspection organizations hire people who can perform NDE; ASNT certification is often the door into the qualifying job.

More questions on API 510 experience

I have 5 years of fab shop welding, mostly structural and some pressure piping. Does that count toward API 510?

Structural welding does not fit API's pressure vessel wording, pressure piping fits API 570 better than API 510, and API requires qualifying experience to be gained with an authorized inspection agency, which a fab shop usually is not. You will also need one year of inspection activities. API decides each application.

Do I need refinery inspection time specifically?

You need one year of supervising or performing inspection activities as described in API 510, gained with an authorized inspection agency such as an owner/user inspection organization or a contractor working for one. That is commonly, but not only, refinery or chemical plant work.

Can a welder with no college degree become a certified pressure vessel inspector?

Yes. API's tiers allow three years of qualifying experience with a high school diploma and five or more with no formal education, each including the one-year inspection floor.

Does military experience count?

API lists three or more years of technical military service as equivalent to a degree for the one-year tier, and two years as equivalent to a two-year degree. Check API's current wording.

Does experience from more than 10 years ago count?

No. API requires qualifying experience within the last 10 years.

Does shop QC on new pressure vessels count as the inspection year?

API 510 is an in-service code, and the inspection year refers to activities as described in API 510. New-construction QC is generally a different activity; describe it accurately and let API judge.

How does API verify my experience?

API states that experience documented on the application will be verified and asks for supervisor contact information.

Which credential can I earn while still welding?

AWS CWI counts welding experience, ASNT method certification is employer-based, and API 577 accepts petrochemical industry experience. Each can help you get hired into an inspection organization.
